results.fact: Approach/camp line: King Lake + east-ridge notch vs. Buck Creek Pass + Liberty Cap + Louis Creek Basin
results.evidence: Both lines are real, documented routes: one source describes climbing from King Lake directly south to a notch (~7,140 ft) on the east ridge, crossing to the south side and contouring onto the low-angle SE slopes to the middle summit (the beta/pitch_detail/itinerary line); other sources describe the long 'normal' route to the west side via Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass high route to a Louis Creek Basin camp (the approach/descent_text/approach_variants line), and note King Lake is also used for the NE face. The row welds two different routes together; choosing which one this route id represents means rewriting beta, pitch_detail, three itinerary days and timing notes (or the approach, descent_text and waypoints), an editorial decision rather than a single wrong value, so no patch is written. Several waypoint pins (the basin and snowfield pins) also sit east of the summit near Trinity, matching neither line.

results.fact: Total elevation gain — 5,300 ft (gain_ft) vs 8,400 ft (itinerary sum) vs 7,300+ ft (approach prose)
results.correct_value: About 8,600 ft round trip from the Snow Lakes trailhead.
results.evidence: The net rise alone is ~7,340 ft (trailhead ~1,300 ft to the 8,638 ft summit). One source tallies ~4,500 ft to Snow Lakes, ~4,500 ft more from Snow Lakes to the summit and back, and ~450 ft on the walk out (~9,450 ft total); another measures ~7,000 ft of gain from the Snow Lakes trailhead just to Aasgard Pass, implying ~6,000 ft to the core-lakes camp. The row's itinerary days (6,000 + 2,300 + regained dips) and the approach's '7,300+' agree against gain_ft 5,300; the itinerary's in/out asymmetry (300 ft lost on the way in, only 100 regained on the way out) is squared so gain and loss both total 8,600.

results.fact: Overnight camp location/elevation — 'Basin below Cannon' at 6,200 ft (waypoints) vs Perfection/Inspiration Lake at ~7,500 ft (itinerary/approach)
results.evidence: Research agrees the camp for this Snow Lakes/Prusik Pass line is in the core Enchantment lakes near Perfection/Inspiration Lake (itinerary, bivy, approach, and route descriptions that reach Prusik Pass from the north end of Perfection Lake). But the 'Basin below Cannon' Campsite pin (and the 'Base of south slopes' pin) sit north-northeast of the summit, on the far side of the mountain from this route, so renaming or re-elevating it would label a pin at the wrong place; pin positions are out of scope. Lake elevations are also unsettled: one mapping source puts Perfection Lake at 7,556 ft (the waypoint's value), others at ~7,000-7,170 ft, so the itinerary's '~7,500 ft' and bivy's 7,190 ft cannot be reconciled from two agreeing sources.

results.fact: Descent trailhead — same Eightmile Road lot with no shuttle needed, vs a different (Stuart Lake) trailhead requiring a car shuttle
results.correct_value: The route starts at the Stuart Lake (Colchuck Lake) trailhead at the end of Eightmile Road (FR 7601) and the loop descends via Aasgard Pass and Colchuck Lake back to that same lot; no car shuttle.
results.evidence: Two independent trip reports of this route both start at the Stuart/Colchuck Lake trailhead (Mountaineer Creek), leave the trail near the Mountaineer Creek bridge or up an old road and climb east to the northeast ridge, then descend toward Prusik Pass, through the upper Enchantments and down Aasgard Pass back to the same trailhead and car. The row's own approach and road driveNote also put the start at the road-end lot. So the 'descent' field is correct, and the fields naming a separate 'Eightmile Trailhead' start and calling for a car shuttle are wrong.

Best attempted only by strong, experienced parties, with a car shuttle or road connection arranged between the two trailheads.
